frontier.hypothesis: The residual is now a global.c CONFLICT-SET problem with a precise two-part target: the island-input copy's allocno must conflict with the `scale` allocno (seated $3) so $3 closes to it, and the `log2_val` allocno must stop conflicting with the `sum_sq` allocno so those two can share $5. Solving only one of the two moves a different insn and holds or worsens the floor (measured: dropping the staging solves the second alone and costs 4 insns).
frontier.mechanism: global.c find_reg scans ascending with no REG_ALLOC_ORDER on MIPS, so a seat is decided purely by which hard regs the allocno's conflicting allocnos already hold; and the allocation order printed in the greg dump (`98 78 120 77 99 ...`) means log2_val's preference for $4 is honoured before sum_sq and the copy are considered.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/ra_solver/inverse.py global on the tied chassis (s6/t0.c / rejected/tied-copy-dowhile-wrap-copy-seats-v1-not-a0-equal-floor-7.c) with a goal seating the copy at 4, log2_val at 5 and sum_sq at 5, --depth 3, and tools/ra_solver/inverse_compose.py classify with --target-object/--ours-object to confirm the residual is RA and not PRE-RA on this chassis. Then spell the top-ranked non-forbidden vector. Re-extract the model first (tools/ra_solver/extract.py + local_extract.py) because the pseudo numbering quoted in evidence.md comes from the s6 diagnostic build, not from the tied build.

frontier.hypothesis: `scale` can be made to conflict with the island-input copy by an ordinary-C change to WHERE scale is written, without adding an insn: e.g. writing the shared tail `scale = ((log2_val << 6) / 500) + 0xC0;` into both inner arms (duplicated-statement-into-arms, a sanctioned family) changes scale's live range and the merge structure.
frontier.mechanism: global.c builds conflicts from allocno live ranges; scale is currently dead across the whole else arm (it is assigned only at the arm's end), which is exactly why the copy's allocno can share $3 with it. Any form that makes scale live at the island entry closes $3 to the copy.
frontier.next_probe: On the s5 w6 chassis measure: (a) `scale = ...` duplicated into both inner arms with the merge label removed; (b) `scale` given a pre-chain default write; (c) `scale` split into a per-arm local copied out at the merge. Score each with `sandbox func_80018094 --disable all` and read the `;; NN conflicts:` line for the copy's allocno in the .greg dump after each - the conflict line, not the score, is the decision variable.

frontier.hypothesis: The tied asm output operand (`: "=m"(sp_tmp[0]), "=r"(lz_in) : "1"(sum_sq)`) on the authorized canonical LZC island is still UNCLASSIFIED - it declares an output the island's text never writes, purely so GCC materialises the input copy. It is not covered by any family in .claude/rules/, so any candidate-ready on the w6 lineage needs a ruling first.
frontier.mechanism: T1 (semantic purpose) and T2 (human-programmer) questions, not a family question: the operand has no observable effect on the function's output, and a reader would ask why the island declares an output register it never assigns.
frontier.next_probe: Grep docs/reference/sotn-construct-index.md for tied / multi-output inline-asm operand precedent among PSX (untagged) entries. If there is none, emit a ruling-request asking whether an authorized canonical-asm island may carry a tied "=r"/"1" operand pair whose only effect is to materialise a copy the target itself contains. Do this BEFORE spending a session driving the w6 lineage to zero.
